question.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve  $y=\frac{5}{x}-2x$ at the point $(1,3)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{5}{x}-2x.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5}{x}-2x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{-1}-2x) \\  & =-5{x}^{-2}-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(1)=-5(1)^{-2}-2=-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(3) & =-7(x-1) \\ y & =-7x+7+3 \\ y & =-7x+10.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-7(0)+10 \\ y & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(0,10).$
